script: This disaster sounds like a joke - it isn't. In 1919, a giant molasses tank burst in Boston, releasing 2 million gallons after a fast temperature swing weakened the steel. The wave was up to 40 feet high, moving 35 miles per hour - faster than people could run. It flattened city blocks. 21 people died, and it's still one of America's deadliest industrial disasters - people just can't stop laughing at the name.

metadata.title: Random But True: The Great Molasses Flood That Actually Killed People
metadata.caption:
A flood of molasses actually killed 21 people in Boston in 1919 - yes, that molasses.

A storage tank holding 2 million gallons suddenly burst, and investigators concluded a rapid temperature swing had weakened the steel past its limit.

The wave that came out was up to 40 feet high and moved around 35 miles per hour - fast enough to outrun someone on foot.

It's still ranked among America's deadliest industrial disasters, and it still sounds like a punchline every time someone hears the name.

Comment if you'd never heard of this one before today.
